children: By Utkarsh    Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nasdaq futures fell more than 1% on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the high-profile listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns, while hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment.
Anthropic
shares slid 7.4% in premarket trading after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut. The stock began trading more than 34% above its offer price of $83.
Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's
earnings this week were seen as key tests of whether battered investor confidence in the AI trade could recover.

But neither revived enthusiasm after weeks of concern about the profitability of massive AI infrastructure spending, rising borrowing costs, regulatory risks following Democrats' win in the US midterm elections, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure.
"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."
As of Thursday's close, the Nasdaq
was 13.6% below its October 6 record closing high, while the S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
had posted its sixth consecutive loss, its longest losing streak since April 2024.
The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.
Among hyperscalers, Amazon
and Microsoft
declined more than 1.5% each, while Meta
fell 2% and Alphabet
was muted. Amazon and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.
Nvidia fell 2.2%, while  Advanced Micro Devices
, Broadcom
, Marvell
, and Micron
lost between 2.2% and 6.6%.
Neoclouds CoreWeave
and Nebius
also dropped about 5% each.
Data center stocks IREN
, Applied Digital
and Core Scientific
fell about 4% each.
At 7:03 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were down 48 points, or 0.1%, and S&P 500 E-minis
were down 53.5 points, or 0.74%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis
were down 436 points, or 1.64%.
The CBOE Volatility Index
, Wall Street's fear gauge, hit the 30-point mark for the first time since March 30.
The selloff in AI-linked stocks has largely overshadowed a strong earnings season.

Of the 462 companies in the S&P 500 to have reported results through Wednesday, 83.5% beat analyst earnings expectations, according to an analysis from Tajinder Dhillon, head of earnings and equity research at LSEG Data and Analytics.
INFLATION, FED IN FOCUS

Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the Fed will need to raise interest rates again because inflation is too high, while arguing that shared understanding matters more than explicit guidance on the rate outlook.
Markets are pricing in a 98.4% chance of an interest rate hike from the central bank at its next meeting in December, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Next week's personal consumption expenditures (PCE) figures will provide further clarity on the Fed's monetary policy path after a hotter-than-expected October inflation report last week.
Among other movers, Intuit
shares fell 9.7% after the company cut its annual revenue growth forecast and agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons
for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times as much.
Futures down: Dow 0.1%, S&P 500 0.74%, Nasdaq 1.64%
